https://entire.io/gh/elviskahoro/native/trails/74
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

**Detail bug report:** [View on Detail](https://app.detail.dev/org_d38a878f-9df9-4c4b-a96a-f5180b860085/bugs/bug_aafdfaf2-a64c-4e0c-a4be-93053a71b8ed)

Closes #108

## Bug
`TabsTrigger.create` ran once at template-build time and baked a generated `id` and the per-item `value` Var into inline `rx.call_script` JS — `document.getElementById('{trigger_id}')`, `root.dataset.value = '{value}'`, and `... === '{value}'`. When a trigger is rendered more than once (via `rx.foreach` or by placing one instance in multiple positions), every copy shares one literal id and one JS body in which the `value` Var has been interpolated as its placeholder name (e.g. `'item_rx_state_'`). The failure has two independent parts:

- Duplicate DOM ids — `getElementById` always resolves to the first copy, so clicks route to the wrong tab.
- Baked value literal — `root.dataset.value` is set to a Var-placeholder string that matches no trigger, so no trigger ever becomes `data-active="true"` and no content panel shows.

Net effect: tabs built from a data list silently do nothing on click, no tab is ever highlighted, and the page has invalid HTML (duplicate ids). The report also notes the same build-time-baking bug class is already documented on `MenuItem` in `components/ui/menu.py`, but Tabs had no warning and — unlike menu — passing an explicit `id` cannot fix it because the baked `'{value}'` literal is a second, independent breakage.

`TabsContent`'s `group-data-[value='{value}']/tabs:block` toggle class is unaffected: `cn()` unwraps it into a runtime Var concat, so content panels stay per-item; they just need the root's `data-value` to be set to the runtime per-item value (which the fix below restores).

## Fix
`components/ui/tabs.py` now powers highlight from a single delegated `document` `click` listener instead of per-trigger `call_script`, mirroring the idiom already used by `components/ui/menu.py` (`MenuRoot` + `__menuGlobalHandlersAttached`):

- `TabsRoot.create` attaches a `GLOBAL_HANDLERS_JS` script on `on_mount` (guarded by `window.__tabsGlobalHandlersAttached` so it's added once per page). The listener resolves the clicked trigger from the real DOM event target via `e.target.closest('[data-slot="tabs-trigger"]')` and reads the runtime value via `getAttribute('data-value')` — no build-time id, no baked value literal. The same script runs a mount pass that marks every trigger against its own root's `data-value` (via `closest('[data-slot="tabs"]')`), so foreach triggers all get their initial `data-active` regardless of `on_mount` being hoisted out of the compiled `.map()`.
- `TabsTrigger.create` no longer generates an `id`, no longer injects highlight `call_script` into `on_click`/`on_mount`. The nested-scope guard from #26 is preserved inside the global handler.
- A delegated listener is used (rather than the report's suggested `event.currentTarget` inside `call_script`) because `rx.call_script` evaluates its JS via `eval()` after a server round-trip, where the DOM `event` is not in scope; a real `addEventListener('click', ...)` is the only place `event` is available.

Docs: updated `docs/components/tabs.md` (`tabs.trigger` description + the `id` default row, `_Auto-generated UUID_` → `_None_`) and regenerated the committed asset `assets/docs/components/tabs.md`.

## Testing
- Unit tests, lint (`ruff check`), format (`ruff format --check`), module boundaries (`tach check`), and `pyrefly check` all pass; the doc-asset sync tests (`test_generated_assets.py`, `test_docs_error.py`) pass and `generate_markdown.py` is idempotent against the change. `pyrefly` reports 4 `bad-override` errors on `components/ui/tabs.py`, all pre-existing on HEAD (verified by `git stash && pyrefly check`); no new typecheck errors.
- `tests/test_tabs.py` adds regression tests for the foreach/duplicate-instance failure (no auto-id, no internal per-trigger JS, runtime-DOM read in the global handler, user-supplied `on_click`/`on_mount` passthrough, foreach-like groups independently switchable) plus direct substring assertions on `GLOBAL_HANDLERS_JS`. Existing nested-scope + flat-demo tests are kept and updated to snapshot by trigger `data-value` (demos no longer set ids).
- Compiled-foreach inspection: compiled a `rx.foreach` tabs page through Reflex's in-process compiler (`App._compile_page` + `component.render()`). The materialised trigger has no `id` prop and `data-value` is the runtime loop Var (not a baked literal); the root `on_mount` payload is the global handler with no `getElementById`, `{value}`, or `{trigger_id}`.
- Browser smoke (Playwright, Chromium headless) against a live Reflex dev server, with a temporary `/probe-foreach` page rendering a `rx.foreach` over a static list (same single-`create()`-shared-across-items structure as a State-Var foreach, verified via the compile above):
  - foreach: 4 roots render, no duplicate trigger ids (all empty), mount marks each root's own default trigger active and shows the matching content panel, clicking a trigger in one root switches only that root (other roots untouched) and the matching content panel becomes visible — 20/20 assertions pass.
  - static `tabs_basic` demo: mount highlights the default, clicking each non-disabled trigger swaps active + visible content correctly.
  - nested tabs probe: inner click switches inner only; outer click switches outer only and preserves the inner value; returning outer restores the inner highlight — the #26 nested-scope guard still holds.
  - icon demo: dispatching a bubbling `MouseEvent` on the `<svg>` inside a trigger activates that trigger (the `e.target.closest` climb works).
  - Before/after proof: re-running the foreach smoke against the original buggy `components/ui/tabs.py` (HEAD) scores 13/20 — the exact bug surfaces (3 build-time ids repeated 4× across the foreach copies, mount marks only the first group's trigger, a click on root[1]'s trigger resolves via `getElementById` to root[0] and switches the wrong group). Restoring the fix returns to 20/20, while the F/nested/G smokes pass on both versions (no regression).
- Could not verify: `reflex _compile()` writing `.web/*.tsx` files — its formatter step requires `bun`, which wasn't available (`npm` alone was insufficient). Worked around by emitting the same structure via Reflex's own `App._compile_page()` + `component.render()`, which is the authoritative source the TSX writer consumes. The foreach cross-browser smokes (Playwright `firefox`/`webkit`) were not exercised; only `chromium` was installed. `rx.foreach` over a freshly-defined `rx.State` Var hit an unrelated Reflex dev-mode SSR failure (`StateContexts.<state>` undefined at `useContext` inside the compiled `Foreach`), so a static-list foreach was used for the browser smoke instead (identical compiled structure, verified above).
